pairs.evidence: crates/agent/src/main.rs:52 The agent refuses to start only when the binary is missing. The auth answer, itself inferred from a credential file, is printed and never acted on, so an unauthorized device still leases relay tasks and burns attempts.

techniques.evidence: crates/agent/src/main.rs:52 Only installation gates work. Authorization (file-existence based, from the shared probe) does not.
crates/agent/src/main.rs:54 A relay action has no deterministic stand-in, so honest refusal is the right rung. It happens before leasing and names the cause and the fix.

crates/agent/src/main.rs:41 Device keys and connector secrets are loaded into the process environment, and every claude child inherits them. Readonly-scan and edit runs over cloud-supplied payloads get those secrets too, because the door strips only ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. The technique asks for a built allowlist environment for children that read untrusted content.

crates/agent/src/exec.rs:168 exec.rs:140 does check out.ok(), and the subtype is surfaced. But an envelope with a missing or empty `result` settles `succeeded` with empty text, so an empty answer reads as success.

crates/agent/src/exec.rs:100 action.toml permission_mode is passed through verbatim, and the seam refuses nothing non-empty, so `bypassPermissions` is accepted for edit. Edit does sit behind an opt-in workspaces_root that defaults to unset.
crates/agent/src/exec.rs:96 One fresh invocation per leased task. No session id is stored or resumed (grep for resume/session_id in crates/agent/src found nothing).

pairs.evidence: crates/engine/src/providers.rs:371 When ANTHROPIC_API_KEY happens to be in the host environment, all Anthropic generation silently moves from the claude -p seat to metered Messages API billing. Billing direction is decided by what is ambient in the environment, not by explicit configuration at the door.

techniques.evidence: crates/engine/src/providers.rs:371 The env key's presence chooses metered over seat. That is exactly the precedence accident the technique exists to prevent, even though DECISIONS D9 documents the reason.
crates/engine/src/providers.rs:368 The ladder is inverted: the metered API outranks an available CLI seat. Which rung served a call is not recorded as an explicit label on the outcome.
crates/engine/src/providers.rs:443 An empty CLI answer becomes EmptyCompletion, never success.
crates/engine/src/providers.rs:437 Generation goes through the typed generate seam: no tools, no permission mode, neutral cwd.
crates/engine/src/chat.rs:106 Stateless: the whole conversation is rendered into each prompt, so no thread id is stored.

pairs.registryProposal: fallback-ladder puts the local CLI seat as rung 1 on economics. This repo measured (D9) about 40k tokens of auto-loaded context per claude -p call and chose the bare API when a key exists. The technique could say the rung order follows measured per-call economics and must be explicit configuration, not fixed CLI-first.
